name: @atlasbound/decisionbook
description: DecisionBook: the history of why beside git's history of what, as plain append-only files a team commits; a readiness rubric, a gate, resume.

verbs.what: choose what needs a plan before an AI session edits it: protect <path or glob>[,...]; --source the source folders; --none nothing; with no word, what you could choose
how to plan before code: one atlasbound decisionbook new in your AI session
<record>, or the JSON on standard input: start a plan: {"title", "why", "success", "kind", "level": micro|normal|critical, "records": [<record>, ...]}; says the state it left

<id> <record> | <id> [<record>, ...], or the JSON on standard input: append one record, or a JSON array of them in one call, all or none: research (a run probe too), a question, a decision, an assumption, the person's confirm, a check, an item (a step too), a link, a waiver, a note; READY when complete, says the state
<id>: READY at the level code decides, else each missing row
<id> [node...] | <type:value>: one plan (in full once a session, then its node map; a node: field[.key|order|index]), or a file, decision, issue, test or commit with its links both ways
<path|words>: the earlier plans of an area: the files, their folder and imports, the same concerns; none named: what the branch changed
<path|words>: the plan pack of an area: its binding decisions, assumptions no person confirmed, check commands, files, the level and what READY needs there, the two calls
what a new session on this branch receives
<id>: record what shipped: its own commits, files and tests
READY or not, and why. The plan-before-code part answers it; an install without that part says package-not-installed
the plan part the next session on this branch would receive (settled decisions, open questions). An install without the plan-before-code part says package-not-installed
